Planning a week of affordable, nutritious family dinners doesn’t have to be a source of stress or a drain on your wallet. With a little strategy and a focus on versatile ingredients, you can serve delicious meals that keep everyone full and healthy without breaking the bank. The key lies in smart shopping, batch cooking, and embracing seasonal produce.

Start by auditing your pantry and freezer. Before you head to the store, check what you already have. This prevents impulse buys and reduces waste. When you do shop, stick to a list. Focus on whole foods, which are generally cheaper and healthier than processed alternatives. Buy meat in bulk and freeze portions for later use, or consider plant-based proteins like lentils, beans, and chickpeas, which are incredibly cheap and packed with fiber and protein.

Next, plan your menu around a "hub and spoke" strategy. Choose one main protein or base ingredient for the week and create different meals around it. For example, if you buy a large bag of brown rice, you can use it for a Monday stir-fry, a Tuesday burrito bowl, and a Wednesday fried rice. This minimizes shopping trips and ensures you use everything you buy.

Batch cooking is your best friend for saving time and money. On Sunday
